item.answer: To make the stock, put the bones in a large pot with two onions, a carrot, a stick of celery and a few peppercorns, cover with cold water and bring slowly to the boil. Skim off the grey foam as it rises, then turn the heat down until the surface barely trembles and leave it for three hours. Strain it through a fine sieve, let it cool, and lift off the fat once it has set.

item.answer: To make the stock, put the bones in a large pot with two onions, a carrot, a stick of celery and a few peppercorns, cover with cold water and bring slowly to the boil. Skim off the grey foam as it rises, then turn the heat down until the surface barely trembles and leave it for three hours. Strain it through a fine sieve, let it cool, and lift off the fat once it has set. The stock will keep for four days in a cold larder, or it can be boiled down by half and stored in small jars. Never salt it at this stage: the sauces made from it will be reduced again, and what tastes right in the pot will be far too strong on the plate.

item.answer: The survey party left the valley before dawn, carrying the theodolite in its padded case and the chain in two canvas bags. By the time the sun cleared the ridge they had set the first station on a flat stone above the river, and the youngest of them was sent down to hold the staff at the ford. The readings were taken twice, as the rule required, once with the telescope direct and once reversed, and the two were entered side by side in the field book so that any disagreement would show at once. At noon they ate bread and cheese in the shade of a wall and argued about whether the old map could be trusted.

item.answer: To make the stock, put the bones in a large pot with two onions, a carrot, a stick of celery and a few peppercorns, cover with cold water and bring slowly to the boil. Skim off the grey foam as it rises, then turn the heat down until the surface barely trembles and leave it for three hours. Strain it through a fine sieve, let it cool, and lift off the fat once it has set. The stock will keep for four days in a cold larder, or it can be boiled down by half and stored in small jars. Never salt it at this stage: the sauces made from it will be reduced again, and what tastes right in the pot will be far too strong on the plate.

item.answer: To make the stock, put the bones in a large pot with two onions, a carrot, a stick of celery and a few peppercorns, cover with cold water and bring slowly to the boil. Skim off the grey foam as it rises, then turn the heat down until the surface barely trembles and leave it for three hours. Strain it through a fine sieve, let it cool, and lift off the fat once it has set. The stock will keep for four days in a cold larder, or it can be boiled down by half and stored in small jars. Never salt it at this stage: the sauces made from it will be reduced again, and what tastes right in the pot will be far too strong on the plate.
